Iris (Customer): Hey team — we're seeing mid-stream truncation when our iOS app goes background and then comes back. The stream starts, we get several chunks, then after background/foreground we only see a partial final chunk (no final newline/terminator) and the client reports connection closed. This is reproducible ~8/10 times when the app background period is >15s. iOS 15.7, app uses our RN WebView + Redwood JS SDK 1.3.2. Ticketing this because it's causing partial content for end users.

Samira (Support): Ack, sorry about that. Can you paste the client-side logs for one of the repro runs and confirm whether you see a 200 from the server before the partial data? Also does the client attempt a reconnect (last-event-id)? :thinking_face:

Iris (Customer): Logs snippet attached (redacted):
```
[SSE] GET /v1/streams/resp 200 OK content-type: text/event-stream
[SSE] data: {"delta":"Here is the start..."}
[SSE] data: {"delta":"...continuation..."}
[SSE] data: {"delta":"...partial-final"}
[SSE] socket: read error ECONNRESET
[SSE] client: reconnect attempt (last-event-id: none)
```
We don't see a final `data: [DONE]` or similar. No request-id in logs here but can enable.

Samira (Support): Thanks — that ECONNRESET + missing DONE suggests the TCP was closed mid-stream (likely OS/network). Quick asks: 1) can you reproduce with `curl --no-buffer` from the device (or from a laptop while toggling wifi) so we can isolate mobile WebView vs server? 2) confirm SDK version (you said 1.3.2). We'll capture the server request-id when you repro so we can correlate.

Jun (Mobile SDK): FWIW iOS will throttle network timers and sometimes pause backgrounded WebViews, which prevents our periodic heartbeat from being written. On iOS the app can get suspended and the socket can be closed by the OS without a graceful shutdown. Heartbeats we send (we currently write a `:ping\n\n` every 15s) won't run reliably in background. Two mitigation options:
- short term: include an id/offset with each chunk (resume_token) so client can ask server to resume from last offset on reconnect (last-event-id-style).
- medium: add native-level background mode for long-running streams (not ideal, often rejected by App Store).
- fallback: use WebSocket fallback which resumes better across network flips.

Jun (Mobile SDK): Example header we can accept on reconnect: `Last-Event-ID: <resume_token>` and server returns the remaining content. Server-side also needs to persist recent partials for a small window (30s-60s).

Max (SRE): We can do a few things server-side: 1) increase grace windows for mid-stream client reconnects and keep partial output cached keyed by resume_token for 45s; 2) emit explicit `retry: 3000` and server-side heartbeat comment lines so well-behaved clients try sooner; 3) log a short request life-cycle ID and emit it as `X-Req-Id` in initial SSE comment so clients can include it in repro (makes triage much faster).

Samira (Support): For immediate repro/help, please try this from a laptop to mimic the phone background behavior:
```bash
# open stream and then flip wifi off/on after ~20s
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/your-stream" --no-buffer
```
If you see the socket close with ECONNRESET after removing wifi, note the exact time and paste server request-id if present. Also enable debug logs in SDK by setting `REDWOOD_SDK_LOG=debug` so we get last-event-id handling details.

Iris (Customer): Will try tomorrow morning. For context we're shipping a live-collab feature; users background the app frequently. We're seeing many such truncated outputs in production (not just dev) so want a robust fix. We're on RN 0.71 + WebView 11.0.x.

Jun (Mobile SDK): If you can share the SDK logs, I can patch the client to send `Last-Event-ID` automatically when reconnecting. Short term we can also change the JS SDK to emit a small local buffer flush on `visibilitychange` so we at least flush what we have to local storage, then retry fetch on resume.

Samira (Support): Summary / next steps — 1) Iris will run the curl repro and capture server request-id + pcap. 2) Jun will prepare a lightweight SDK patch to attach resume tokens on each chunk and auto-send Last-Event-ID on reconnect for RN/JS SDKs. 3) Max will prototype a short-lived partial-output cache keyed by resume_token on the streaming infra and add `X-Req-Id` header in initial response. 4) I'll keep this thread updated and create an escalation ticket. Assigning to SRE + Mobile SDK to coordinate. :+1:

oncall-bot: Escalation created: RT-12345 — Priority P2. Linked: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/RT-12345

Iris (Customer): Thanks all — I'll attach logs and the pcap when I have them. Appreciate the quick triage. :pray:
